findings.name: Veteran's Property Tax Exemption
findings.description: Wyoming provides a $6,000 reduction in assessed value against real or personal property (e.g., vehicle licensing fees, if not applied to real property) for honorably discharged veterans of WWI, WWII, Korea, or Vietnam, or veterans awarded the Armed Forces Expeditionary Medal or another authorized service/campaign medal for foreign service, provided the veteran is a current Wyoming resident who has lived in the state for three years. Certain disabled veterans may also be eligible per department statutes and rules. Surviving spouses may continue to collect the exemption until remarriage. Application deadline is the fourth Monday in May, filed with the County Assessor, with annual contact required.
findings.value: $6,000 reduction in assessed value against real or personal property
otherReqs: Current Wyoming resident, lived in-state for 3 years
Honorable discharge from WWI, WWII, Korea, Vietnam, or awarded a qualifying expeditionary/campaign medal for foreign service
Surviving spouse may continue to collect until remarriage
Must contact the County Assessor annually
findings.agency: Wyoming Department of Revenue / County Assessor
documentation: DD-214 or proof of honorable discharge and qualifying service/medal
findings.sourceExcerpt: The program provides $6000 in assessed value against real - personal property for qualifying veterans and surviving spouses. Applicants must be a current Wyoming resident and must have lived in the state for three years. Application deadline is the fourth Monday in May for the property tax exemption.

findings.name: Purple Heart Recipient Free Lifetime Hunting/Fishing License
findings.description: Wyoming residents who are U.S. Military Purple Heart Medal recipients receive lifetime game bird, small game, and fish licenses free of charge. Acceptable proof includes an official DD-214, a VA Veterans Identification Card with Purple Heart Medal designation, or a U.S. Purple Heart Medal Recipient certificate.
findings.value: Free lifetime game bird, small game, and fish license
otherReqs: Proof of Purple Heart award required (DD-214, VA VIC with Purple Heart designation, or Purple Heart certificate)
documentation: DD-214, VA Veterans Identification Card with Purple Heart designation, or Purple Heart Medal Recipient certificate
findings.sourceExcerpt: U.S. Military Purple Heart Medal recipients who are Wyoming residents receive lifetime game bird, small game, and fish licenses issued without charge. Statute: Wyoming State Statute Section 23-1-705(d). Acceptable proof includes Official DD-214 form, VA VIC with Purple Heart Medal designation, or Purple Heart Medal Recipient certificate.

findings.name: 100% Disabled Veteran Bird, Fish and Small Game License
findings.description: Wyoming resident veterans who are honorably discharged and hold a letter from the VA certifying a 100% disability rating (based on actual disability, not compensation level) may obtain a 100% Disabled Veteran Bird, Fish and Small Game License. Holders of this license are exempt from the requirement to purchase a conservation stamp while exercising hunting or fishing privileges under any Wyoming license. Separately, veterans with a 50% or greater VA service-connected disability compensation rating may obtain a 50% Disabled Veteran Fishing License, valid for the holder's lifetime.
findings.value: 100% disability tier: bird/fish/small game license plus conservation-stamp exemption; 50% disability tier: lifetime fishing license
otherReqs: 100% tier requires a VA letter certifying actual (not compensation-based) 100% disability
findings.sourceExcerpt: To be eligible for a 100% Disabled Veteran Bird, Fish and Small Game License, you must be a honorably discharged resident of Wyoming and have a letter from the Department of Veterans Affairs certifying to the 100% level of disability. Persons holding this license are exempt from the requirement to purchase a conservation stamp. The 50% Disabled Veteran Fishing License is valid for the lifetime of the person holding it.

findings.name: Disabled Veteran License Plates
findings.description: Wyoming veterans may apply for military-related license plates through the County Treasurer's Office by providing a DD Form 214 confirming Wyoming residency and veteran status. A separate application exists specifically for disabled veteran plates.
findings.value: Disabled Veteran license plate available through the County Treasurer's Office
findings.sourceExcerpt: Military-Related License Plates available through County Treasurer's Office; requires Wyoming residency and veteran status with DD Form 214. Separate application for disabled veteran plates exists (Disabled Veteran Plates application).

findings.name: Public Employment Preference for Veterans
findings.description: Wyoming grants honorably discharged veterans (and eligible surviving spouses) an interview preference in every public department, including the state and its branches, agencies, municipalities, counties, school districts, political subdivisions, special districts, community college districts, and the University of Wyoming. When a public department uses a numerical scoring system prior to its interview process, a veteran or surviving spouse receives a 5% advantage over any non-veteran applicant. Disabled veterans receive preference over able-bodied veterans if the disability does not materially interfere with performance of the duties. No preference is given to a veteran currently employed by the public department.
findings.value: Interview preference plus a 5% scoring advantage over non-veteran applicants at Wyoming public departments
otherReqs: Honorably discharged Wyoming resident of one year or more before applying (or eligible surviving spouse)
Must possess business capacity, competency, education, or other qualifications required for the position
No preference for veterans currently employed by the department
findings.agency: State of Wyoming and its political subdivisions
documentation: Proof of veteran status (DD-214) or, for surviving spouses, proof of marriage and federal survivor benefits
findings.sourceExcerpt: Whenever a veteran or surviving spouse applies for initial employment with a public department that uses a numerical scoring system prior to its interview process, the veteran or surviving spouse shall be allowed a five percent (5%) advantage over any nonveteran. Honorably discharged veterans who have been Wyoming residents for one year or more before applying are eligible.
